D009-D008_h001.question:
I’ve been feeling really down for about a year now—just constantly sad, empty, like nothing matters. I don’t enjoy going to work, and I used to love grooming animals. Now, even playing with my own dog doesn’t make me smile. Everything feels like effort, especially thinking or focusing—I get mentally exhausted just trying to follow a conversation. Some days, I catch myself thinking, *I just don’t want to wake up*, not because I have a plan, but because it all feels too heavy.

But then, for about a month last fall, it was like the opposite. I was buzzing—super talkative, so fast people would say, “Whoa, slow down!” I’d stay up until 3 a.m. cleaning my apartment or texting friends, but I still felt great in the morning. I remember pacing while on calls, twirling my hair, tapping my feet—just couldn’t sit still. I felt kind of high, maybe excited one minute, then snapping at a coworker the next for no reason. But I kept up with work, no complaints. It didn’t ruin anything, really. Just felt like a strange, restless energy I couldn’t explain.
D009-D008_h001.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D009-D008_h001.answer: C & B. Bipolar II Disorder & Bipolar I Disorder

D009-D008_h002.question:
I’ve been feeling so down for about a year now—just no joy in anything, really. My daughter stopped by less often, and I can’t say I blame her; I don’t even feel like answering the phone. I used to take pride in keeping the house tidy, baking for the neighbors, but now it’s all just… too much. I don’t have the energy to get out of my chair most days, and when I do, it’s like my body’s made of lead. Thoughts cross my mind—wish I could just go to sleep and not wake up—but I’m not going to do anything about it. I wouldn’t want to burden anyone like that.

But before this low, I had this odd spell—lasted around a month—where I was cleaning cabinets at 2 a.m., rearranging photo albums, calling old friends out of the blue. I’d talk and talk, even if they didn’t answer. I wasn’t tired, not at all. I’d pace the kitchen, wring my hands, start three projects at once. My mood? One minute I’d feel cheerful, like I’d solved everything, and then something small—a dropped spoon—would set me off. It wasn’t normal, but I don’t know if it was dangerous either. I never thought I was special or hearing voices—just restless, I guess.
D009-D008_h002.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D009-D008_h002.answer: C & B. Bipolar II Disorder & Bipolar I Disorder

D009-D008_h003.question:
I’ve been married for twenty years, and I drive the subway—same route, same tunnels, day in and day out. It’s steady, but it can get monotonous. About a year ago, things started shifting. At first, I felt… lighter. Like I’d woken up from a long fog. For about a month, I was buzzing—upbeat, joking with strangers at the terminal, calling friends I hadn’t talked to in years. I’d sleep two or three hours and feel *great*, like I was finally catching up on life. I’d talk nonstop during breaks, even interrupting coworkers, just full of ideas—renovating the house, starting a side gig, all kinds of plans.

But that high faded, and it’s been a slow drain ever since. Now I can barely get out of bed. I don’t want to talk to anyone. The thought of work feels impossible, and some mornings I cry for no reason. I still go in—I can’t afford to lose the job—but I’m just going through the motions. Some nights I think, *Wouldn’t it be easier if I didn’t wake up?* But I’d never act on it. I’m not sure what’s wrong—maybe I’m just worn down. It’s not like I’ve ever lost control completely or needed to be hospitalized. Just… stuck between two extremes, neither one making sense.
D009-D008_h003.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D009-D008_h003.answer: C & B. Bipolar II Disorder & Bipolar I Disorder

D009-D008_h004.question:

    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

I can’t remember a night without bad dreams—falling, being trapped, missing deadlines that spiral into chaos. I wake up panicked, heart racing, and then just lie there dreading sleep. The mood swings? They don’t exactly ruin my work—the light stays on—but I notice the edges fraying. I don’t know if it’s stress, age, or something else. Maybe just being alone out here too long. I wouldn’t say I’m unwell enough to need hospitalizing… but some days, it feels close.

D009-D008_h021.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year—maybe a little more. It started with just feeling flat, like nothing brought me any joy, not even design work, which I’ve always loved. I’d sit in front of my screen for hours and couldn’t focus; even small tasks felt exhausting, like my brain was moving through mud. I felt sad all the time, and my husband said I moved slower than usual—like I was dragging myself through the day.  

Then, about three months ago, something shifted. I wasn’t suddenly happy, but I got this restless energy. I started redesigning our entire app prototype at night, jumping between five projects at once, barely sleeping—sometimes not at all for two or three nights. But I didn’t feel tired. If anything, stopping felt annoying. I got really short-tempered too—snapping at my team over tiny feedback. It wasn’t like I was euphoric or out of control, but I couldn’t sit still, mentally or physically.  

Now the motivation’s fading again, and the heaviness is creeping back. I don’t know if this is just burnout or something more—I’m functioning, but just barely.

D009-D008_h022.question:
Lately—well, really over the past year or so—I’ve just felt… drained. Nothing excites me like it used to. Getting through the day takes everything I have. Even opening emails at work feels overwhelming, and I don’t have the energy to follow through on things I used to handle without thinking. My husband says I’ve become distant, like I’m not really *there*. Emotionally, it’s like I’m wrapped in thick cotton—nothing gets through. I can’t even cry. I pace at home, mostly at night, back and forth in the kitchen. Can’t sit still, even when I’m exhausted.

But before this stretch, things were… different. About three months ago, I hit a burst of energy. I launched three new client initiatives at the branch, reorganized the team schedule, and barely slept—sometimes not until 2 or 3 a.m.—but I didn’t feel tired. I felt sharp, happy, like I could do anything. I wasn’t *risky*, just… unstoppable. Then it faded, and the heaviness came back.

I don’t know if this is burnout, grief, or something else. I’ve managed my job, but it’s been a struggle. Nothing’s ever felt out of control—no one’s suggested I need hospitalization or warned me about psychosis or anything like that. I just keep wondering why I can’t stay steady.

D009-D008_h023.question:
I’ve been... off for quite a while now—over a year, maybe a little more. There are days when everything feels heavy, like my body’s made of concrete. Just getting out of bed takes effort, and walking to the kitchen feels twice as long. Things that used to matter—work, finishing a fix on an old COBOL module—don’t spark anything in me. I just do them, if I do them at all. I don’t care if I succeed. It’s like my emotions are wrapped in cotton. Nothing cuts through.

But then, around three months ago, something shifted. Not all at once—just bursts. I’d wake up at 3 a.m. and start coding, rewriting legacy scripts for systems that haven’t been touched in decades. Felt sharp, alive. Took on three projects at once, stayed up for nights straight—didn’t even notice I wasn’t sleeping. I’d be laughing one minute about some outdated syntax, then snap at my coworker the next for a minor comment. Felt unstoppable, but not crazy. Never felt out of control, not really. People noticed, but I didn’t lose the job or end up in hospital. Just… swung between numb and buzzing, like a current that won’t settle.

D009-D008_h024.question:
I’ve been feeling… off for over a year now. The low moods started first—just this heavy sadness that won’t lift, no matter how much I push through. I used to love coaching clients, planning workouts, even hitting the gym after hours for my own routine. Now? Nothing sparks joy. I drag myself through sessions, but my mind feels stuck, like I’m moving underwater. Talking takes effort—sometimes I know what I want to say, but it comes out slow, delayed. I’m exhausted all the time, even after eight hours of sleep.  

Then, about three months ago, something shifted. Not better—different. I felt like I could take on ten clients at once, sign up for every certification, revamp the whole gym floor. I was irritable, though—small things set me off, like someone touching my equipment or a delayed appointment. I didn’t need much sleep—four or five hours and I was up, pacing, texting plans at 3 a.m. But I didn’t crash. I didn’t miss work. I just felt… revved.  

Now the energy’s fading, and the weight’s coming back. I don’t know if I’m broken or just burnt out. It hasn’t put me in the hospital or anything, but some days, I barely make it through the schedule.

D009-D008_h025.question:
I’ve been feeling low for over a year now—just this constant heaviness, like I’m moving through mud. I don’t find joy in much anymore, not even my garden or the crossword. Some days, getting out of my chair feels like climbing a mountain. My son says I’m slower, and he’s right—I take longer to do simple things, like buttoning my shirt or standing up from the couch. I’m tired all the time, even after a full night’s sleep.

But then, for about the past three months, something shifted—part of me, anyway. I don’t sleep much—maybe four hours a night—but I’m not exhausted. I’m up at dawn, pacing, cleaning cupboards, writing letters I never send. My mood swings without warning: one minute I’m laughing at old war movies, the next I’m snapping at the neighbor over nothing. I can’t sit still, like there’s a motor running under my skin.

It’s not that any of it’s *unmanageable*—I bathe, I eat, I pay the bills—but I know I’m not right. My wife would’ve noticed. I just don’t know if this is grief, old age, or something else altogether.
